title: A simple maximal-ideal root of a polynomial reducing to X
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative henselian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $\kappa$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-residue-field]. Let $H\in R[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] have reduction $\overline H=X$. Then there exists $z\in\mathfrak m$ with $H(z)=0$ and $H^{\prime}(z)\in R^\times$. No monicity, valuation, topology or domain assumption is imposed on $R$ or $H$.

source.place: Tag 04GG, simple-root characterization; explicit reciprocal-polynomial reduction to the monic interface (agent reconstruction of the original stability proof steps 4--5)

proof.text: Put p=H(1-X), N=natDegree(H)+1. Evaluation of the reduction at 1 gives residue(H(1))=1, so H(1) is a unit u. The polynomial Q=C(u inverse)*reflect(N,p) has degree at most N; its coefficient at N is u inverse*p.coeff(0)=1. Thus Q is monic. This is coefficient reflection, with N fixed before reducing coefficients.

source.place: Tag 04GG, simple-root characterization; explicit reciprocal-polynomial reduction to the monic interface (agent reconstruction of the original stability proof steps 4--5)

proof.text: Mapping reflection and composition to the residue field gives Qbar=X^N-X^(N-1). Its value at 1 is zero and its derivative there is N-(N-1)=1 in every characteristic. Apply Mathlib HenselianLocalRing.TFAE, implication 0 to 1, to the monic Q and the residue root 1. Obtain Q(y)=0 and residue(y)=1. This is precisely the monic simple-root interface of the henselian notion [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

source.place: Tag 04GG, simple-root characterization; explicit reciprocal-polynomial reduction to the monic interface (agent reconstruction of the original stability proof steps 4--5)

proof.text: The element y is a unit. Set z=1-y inverse; its residue is zero, so it is in the maximal ideal. Since Q(y)=0, multiplying by u gives reflect(N,p)(y)=0. The reflection evaluation identity at the inverse unit gives p(y inverse)=0, equivalently H(z)=0.

source.place: Tag 04GG, simple-root characterization; explicit reciprocal-polynomial reduction to the monic interface (agent reconstruction of the original stability proof steps 4--5)

proof.text: The derivative commutes with coefficient reduction, so H prime reduces to 1. Consequently residue(H prime(z))=1, and H prime(z) is a unit.

theorem exists_simple_root_of_map_eq_X
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [HenselianLocalRing R]
    (H : R[X]) (hH : H.map (residue R) = X) :
    ∃ z : R, z ∈ maximalIdeal R ∧ H.IsRoot z ∧ IsUnit (H.derivative.eval z)
